skill.name: gsap-timeline
skill.description: Guides GSAP animation sequencing with timelines, position parameters, shared defaults, labels, nested timelines, and playback controls.
skill.summary: Build and control coordinated GSAP animation sequences with practical timeline guidance.
skill.author: greensock

security_audit.summary: All 17 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or inline backticks around GSAP examples. The reviewed SKILL.md contains animation guidance, not shell execution. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, or other intent-level security risks.

static_findings.snippet: - **Placement**: `"<"` — start when recently-added animation starts; `">"` — start when recently-add
- **paused: true** — create paused; call `.play()` to start.
- ✅ Add **labels** with `addLabel()` for readable, maintainable sequencing.
- ❌ Chain animations with **delay** when a **timeline** can sequence them; prefer `gsap.timeline()`

content.value_statement: Coordinating multiple animations becomes difficult when timing depends on separate delays. This skill guides GSAP timeline sequencing with labels, relative positions, shared defaults, and playback controls.
actual_capabilities: Explain sequential tween chaining and absolute, relative, label-based, and previous-animation position parameters.
Guide shared duration and easing defaults for child tweens.
Describe paused construction, repeats, yoyo behavior, and timeline callbacks.
Show label creation, playback from labels, and playhead animation between labels.
Demonstrate child timeline nesting within a master timeline.
Explain play, pause, reverse, restart, time, progress, and kill controls.
limitations: Provides documentation and examples, not an executable animation tool or bundled GSAP runtime.
Does not include automated tests, browser previews, or performance measurements.
Refers to separate skills for detailed single-tween, ScrollTrigger, and React guidance.
Does not cover dependency installation or project setup.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Interface Transitions
use_cases.description: Sequence panel movement, text appearance, and button reveals using shared defaults and relative tween positions.

use_cases.title: Translate Motion Plans into Timelines
use_cases.description: Map animation phases to labels and describe overlaps through explicit timeline positions.
use_cases.target_user: Motion designers who prototype in JavaScript

use_cases.title: Maintain Complex Animation Sequences
use_cases.description: Organize child timelines under a master timeline and identify playback controls for reviewing individual phases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a First Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gsap-timeline to sequence a panel slide, heading reveal, and button fade. Explain how the timeline appends each tween.

prompt_templates.title: Control Overlapping Timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gsap-timeline to start a heading with the previous animation and reveal a button 0.2 seconds later. Apply shared duration and easing defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Add Labels and Playback
prompt_templates.prompt: Add intro and outro labels to my GSAP timeline. Show paused construction, playback from outro, and playhead animation between the labels.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Master Timeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my GSAP sequence for repeated delays and duplicated defaults. Refactor it into nested timelines with labels and explain top-level ScrollTrigger placement.

output_examples.input: Plan a panel entrance, a heading that starts with it, and a button reveal 0.2 seconds after the heading starts.
output: Create one timeline with shared duration and easing defaults.
Align the heading with the start of the previous animation.
Position the button 0.2 seconds after the heading begins.

output_examples.input: Describe a reusable intro sequence inside a master timeline, with playback available from an outro label.
output: Build the intro as a child timeline containing its coordinated tweens.
Insert the child at the start of the master timeline.
Add an outro label and attach the exit animations to it.
Start the master timeline from the outro label when only the exit phase is needed.

best_practices: Use position parameters and descriptive labels to make sequencing explicit.
Set shared duration and easing defaults on the timeline when multiple child tweens use them.
Keep ScrollTrigger on the top-level tween or timeline rather than nested animations.
anti_patterns: Coordinating multi-step animations through independent delays instead of timeline positions.
Repeating identical duration and easing settings across many child tweens.
Treating constructor duration as the duration of each tween or the entire computed timeline.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers GSAP timeline creation, tween placement, shared defaults, labels, nesting, and playback controls.

faq.question: Does the skill install GSAP?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and JavaScript examples, without installation commands or a bundled runtime.

faq.question: How do I make two animations start together?
faq.answer: Use the less-than position marker on the second tween to align its start with the previously added animation.

faq.question: Why should I use labels?
faq.answer: Labels name timeline positions so animations and playback controls can reference readable phases instead of repeated numeric offsets.

faq.question: Does this include React or scroll-driven animation setup?
faq.answer: It refers to separate React and ScrollTrigger skills. Its own scroll-related guidance focuses on keeping ScrollTrigger at the top level.

faq.question: Can I control playback after creating a timeline?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers play, pause, reverse, restart, seeking by time or progress, and killing a timeline.
